stories.headline: CEASE-FIRE TODAY IN ALL JERUSALEM SET BY ARABS, JEWS; Briton Gets Azzam Pasha's Pledge for Halt at Noon -- Food Route Not Affected ZIONISTS CLAIM VILLAGES British Ask U. N. to Name City Commissioner -- Choice of an American Likely TRAINING MEN FOR THE JEWISH ARMY IN PALESTINE CEASE-FIRE TODAY SET IN JERUSALEM
stories.summary: Arabs and Jews agree to a cease-fire in Jerusalem after a conference between Azzam Pasha and Cunningham, with the British asking the UN to appoint a city commissioner

stories.headline: ISRAEL USES FLIERS TO STRIKE IN NORTH; RETIRES IN OLD CITY; Air Force's Initial Blow Hits Samakh Area -- Ground Unit Enters Syria, Razes Depot JERUSALEM BATTLE RAGES Arabs Claim Control of 80% of Walled Area -- Egyptian Troops Seize Beersheba ISRAEL USES FLIERS TO STRIKE IN NORTH A NERW AIR FORCE ENTERS PALESTINE WARFARE
stories.summary: Israel uses air power for the first time, bombing Arab forces near the Galilee Sea, while ground units enter Syria and Egypt seizes Beersheba

stories.headline: 14 OF 23.CONTESTS IN OHIO SHOW TAFT AHEAD OF STASSEN; Senator Leads for All Nine Delegates-at-Large and in 13 District Races TREND SHIFTS POSSIBLE Turnout Is Heavy in the GOP Primary and Count Is Slow -- Lausche Defeats Miller AS THE REPUBLICAN PRIMARY CONTEST IN OHIO NEARED ITS CLOSE YESTERDAY TAFT TAKES LEAD IN OHIO PRIMARY
stories.summary: Robert Taft takes the lead over Harold Stassen in Ohio's Republican primary, with a heavy turnout and slow count

stories.headline: STEELMAN PARLEYS WITH RAIL UNIONS MAKE NO PROGRESS; After 'Exploratory' Talks Fail, Truman Aide Confers Briefly With Faricy, Roads' Leader TO MEET CARRIERS TODAY Their Negotiators Are Called From Chicago -- Truman Meets Cabinet -- No Seizure Move RAIL PEACE TALKS MAKE NO PROGRESS
stories.summary: Truman's aide, Steelman, holds talks with rail unions but makes no progress, as shippers pressure Truman to prevent a strike

rounds.blurb: Israel's declaration of independence sparked conflict with Arab forces. A cease-fire was agreed upon in Jerusalem after a conference between Azzam Pasha and Cunningham. Israel used air power for the first time, bombing Arab forces near the Galilee Sea.

stories.headline: FAUBUS CONTINUES TALKS WITH HAYS; IMPASSE REMAINS; Little Rock School Guarded ----President to Meet Powell to Discuss Integration Hays Seeks a Formula U.S. Prepares Case FAUBUS CONTINUES TALKS WITH HAYS All Is Quiet at School
stories.summary: Orval Faubus continues talks with the US government as the Little Rock school integration crisis remains unresolved, with President Dwight D. Eisenhower set to meet with Adam Powell to discuss the issue. The US prepares a case while Faubus urges the removal of the National Guard from the school.

stories.headline: Survey Finds Blow To G.O.P. in South; Survey Finds Little Rock Dispute a Setback to Republican Efforts to Win South NEGRO VOTE GAINS NEW SIGNIFICANCE Study Asserts Complications Face Democrats in '60 on Presidential Ticket G.O.P. Losses Reported State-wide Effect Noted Dilemma for Democrats Bias Laws a Factor North Carolina Maryland Missouri Alabama Louisiana Split in G.O.P. Ranks Texas Oklahoma Pennsylvania Michigan Illinois California Washington
stories.summary: A survey finds that the Little Rock dispute has hurt Republican efforts to win over the South, particularly among African American voters, as the party faces complications and a dilemma in its approach to the region. The Democratic party also faces challenges in the upcoming presidential election.

stories.headline: BULGANIN WARNS TURKEY TO AVOID ATTACK ON SYRIA; Charges Troops Are Poised on Border to Carry Out Plan Directed by U.S. HINTS ACTION BY SOVIET Says Mideast Military Move Might Bring World War-- Washington Denies Plot Turkey Accused by Gromyko Bulganin Cites Geography BULGANIN WARNS TURKS ON SYRIA Bulganin Appeals to Turkey U.S. Disavows Any Role
stories.summary: Soviet Premier Bulganin warns Turkey not to attack Syria, alleging that the US is planning military action against Syria with Turkey's involvement, and hints that the Soviet Union may take action to prevent this. The US denies any such plans.

stories.headline: U.S. IS STILL COOL TO PLEAS TO JOIN BAGHDAD TREATY; But Is Expected to Weigh Turkey's Bid Again When Henderson Returns
stories.summary: The US remains hesitant to join the Baghdad Treaty, despite pleas from Turkey and Iraq, as the Syrian government drifts towards the left. The US is expected to reconsider Turkey's bid when Henderson returns.

rounds.blurb: Orval Faubus continued talks with the US government as the Little Rock school integration crisis remained unresolved. The dispute hurt Republican efforts to win over the South, particularly among African American voters. Soviet Premier Bulganin warned Turkey not to attack Syria, alleging US involvement.

stories.headline: RITES TOMORROW; Burial in Arlington-- Many World Leaders to Attend Funeral Visits by Ex-Presidents Military Cortege Set Kennedy's Body Lies in White House; Military Cortege to Precede Arlington Burial WORLD LEADES TO ATTEND RITES Funeral Set for Tomorrow --Officials Pay Respects at Bier in White House Private Mass Said McCormack Is First Flowers Discouraged
stories.summary: World leaders gather to pay respects to President Kennedy at the White House before his burial in Arlington, with many attending the funeral

stories.headline: Gov. Connally Shot; Mrs. Kennedy Safe; President Is Struck Down by a Rifle Shot From Building on Motorcade Route-- Johnson, Riding Behind, Is Unhurt Suspect Captured After Scuffle Priests Administer Last Rites Johnson Embraces Mrs. Kennedy Resuscitation Attempted In Operating Room 40 Minutes Kennedys Hailed at Breakfast Approaching 3-Street Underpass Rumors Spread at Trade Mart Mrs. Kennedy's Reaction Eyewitness Describes Shooting Tour by Mrs. Kennedy Unusual
stories.summary: President Kennedy is assassinated and Governor Connally is shot while riding in a Dallas motorcade, with Lyndon B. Johnson riding behind them unhurt

stories.headline: RUSSIANS REPORT LAUNCHING CRAFT THAT SHIFTS ORBIT; Major Advance Is Claimed for Rendezvous in Space --More Shots Predicted KHRUSHCHEV JUBILANT He Expresses Support for a U.S.-Soviet Lunar Trip if Tensions Are Eased Stresses Joint Flights SOVIET LAUNCHES STEERABLE CRAFT Scientists Are Toasted Vagueness Is Cited Forms of Steering Explained
stories.summary: Premier Khrushchev announces a major advance in space rendezvous technology and expresses support for a joint US-Soviet lunar trip if tensions are eased

stories.headline: U.S. RECOGNIZES REGIME IN SAIGON; TALKS ON AID SET; Move Comes Less Than Week After Overthrow of Diem by Military Leaders NEW CLIMATE IS SEEN Hope for Fresh Efforts in War Against Guerrillas Is Signaled by Action 'Mutual Benefit' Sought Note Delivered in Saigon U.S. RECOGNIZES REGIME IN SAIGON Contrast Is Noted
stories.summary: The US recognizes the new regime in Saigon and seeks to renew aid talks, hoping for a fresh effort in the war against guerrillas

rounds.blurb: President Kennedy's assassination occurred while he was riding in a Dallas motorcade. Governor Connally was also shot, and world leaders gathered to pay respects before his burial in Arlington. The US also recognized the new regime in Saigon and made advances in space technology.
